speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: When will the grace-devotion pair take root?
premises: Grace-drop (prasādalava) stationed in the Lord (īśvarasthito); devotion (bhakti) come as if to meet me (iva mām upeyuṣī).
The pair (tau) joined (parasparasamanvitau) — when will they take root (rūḍhim eṣyataḥ) in such a body (tādṛśe vapuṣi)?
The verse poses the meeting as a question, not an assertion: the devotee does not claim the upsurge has happened.
inference: The grace-devotion pair is posed as a question: when will they take root? The devotee does not claim the upsurge; he asks for it.
uncertainties: Whether 'prasādalava' means 'drop of grace' or 'grace's drop' (genitive) is unresolved.
Whether 'tādṛśe vapuṣi' refers to the devotee's body or the Lord's body is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is the first fruit of chewing His lordship?
premises: Born of chewing His lordship (tvatprabhutvaparicarvaṇajanmā): may some inner joy-juice (paritoṣaraso) rise ('ntaḥ udetu).
Here always be supreme for me (sarvakālam iha me param astu) — knowledge-yoga's glories far off (jñānayogamahimādi vidūre).
The verse converts chewing (carvaṇa) into a method: rumination produces joy-juice, displacing metaphysics.
inference: Chewing His lordship produces inner joy-juice; knowledge-yoga's glories are far off. Rumination displaces metaphysics.
uncertainties: Whether 'ko 'pi' (some) refers to joy-juice or to a person is unresolved.
Whether 'param' (supreme) modifies 'astu' or 'me' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: How is worldly thirst redirected?
premises: Like the worldly (lokavad), let my thirst for objects swell (sphīta eva bhagavanparitarṣaḥ).
Only seeing them as Your body (tava śarīratayaitān lokayeyam), unconstructed (astavikalpaḥ).
The verse keeps worldly thirst but redirects it: thirst for objects becomes thirst for seeing them as His body.
inference: Worldly thirst kept, unconstructed sight required: thirst for objects becomes thirst for seeing them as His body.
uncertainties: Whether 'bhagavanparitarṣaḥ' means 'thirst for You, Lord' or 'thirst, O Lord' is unresolved.
Whether 'astavikalpaḥ' means 'unconstructed' or 'without alternative' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: Where is plainness demanded?
premises: In body-grounds (dehabhūmiṣu) and in mind (manasi), Lord (tvaṃ), and in breath's course (prāṇavartmani) where difference (bhedam) has come (upete) —
and in those consciousness-paths (saṃvidaḥ pathiṣu teṣu ca) — by Yourself (tena svātmanā) be plain (sphuṭarūpaḥ) to me (mama).
Plainness demanded in both registers: body-grounds and consciousness-paths.
inference: Plainness demanded in both registers: body-grounds and consciousness-paths. By Yourself, be plain to me.
uncertainties: Whether 'sphuṭarūpaḥ' means 'plain' or 'manifest' is unresolved.
Whether 'tena' refers to Yourself or to the path is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is the one fear?
premises: May these thrilled faculties (imāḥ karaṇavṛttaya ullasitā) fall into their own seats (nijanijeṣu padeṣu patantv).
Never, Lord (kṣaṇamapīśa), even slightly (manāg api), the daring of non-difference-rupture (tvadavibhedarasakṣatisāhasam).
One fear named: rupture of non-difference. The faculties self-seat; the daring is refused.
inference: Faculties self-seat; one fear named — rupture of non-difference. The daring is refused.
uncertainties: Whether 'kṣaṇamapīśa' means 'never, Lord, even for a moment' or 'Lord, even for a moment' is unresolved.
Whether 'tvadavibhedarasa' means 'the rasa of non-difference' or 'the non-difference-rasa' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What exceeds transaction?
premises: Light, soft, white-pure, cool (laghumasṛṇasitācchaśītalaṃ) — contemplating (bhāvayan) by possession-force (bhavadāveśavaśena) a body (vapur).
May I exceed (ativartayeya) those dealings (vyavahārān) of the all-thing-road (akhilapadārthapaddhater).
Possession-body exceeds transaction: the world is left, not refuted.
inference: Possession-body exceeds transaction: the world is left, not refuted. May I exceed those dealings.
uncertainties: Whether 'laghumasṛṇasitācchaśītalaṃ' describes the body or the contemplation is unresolved.
Whether 'vyavahāra' means transaction or worldly dealing is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What becomes untellable?
premises: May my self-body bloom (vikasatu svavapur) as You (bhavadātmakaṃ).
May worlds join (samupayāntu) my limbs (mamāṅgatām).
May all this duality-sport (sarvam idaṃ dvayavalgitaṃ), even recalled (smṛtipathopagame 'py), become untellable (anupākhyatām).
inference: Blooming, joining, untellability: the duality-sport becomes untellable even when recalled.
uncertainties: Whether 'dvayavalgitaṃ' means 'duality-sport' or 'the sport of duality' is unresolved.
Whether 'anupākhyatām' means 'untellable' or 'unnameable' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What fills the dread gorge?
premises: May there rise (samudiyād), looking at such Yours (tādṛśatāvakānana viloka), a flood of supreme nectar (parāmṛtasamplavaḥ).
So my filling (ghaṭeta) of non-duality's dread gorge (bhavadadvayāprathanaghoradarīparipūraṇam) happens (mama).
The abyss is flooded: non-duality's dread gorge filled by supreme nectar.
inference: The abyss is flooded: non-duality's dread gorge filled by supreme nectar. Looking at His, the flood rises.
uncertainties: Whether 'tādṛśatāvakānana' means 'such Yours' or 'such a forest of Yours' is unresolved.
Whether 'ghoradarī' means 'dread gorge' or 'terrible cave' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is the wager?
premises: If ever (api kadācana) by the thinnest union-drops (tāvakasaṅgamāmṛtakaṇācchuraṇena tanīyasā) —
may I turn (parāṅmukho) from all world-pleasures (sakalalokasukheṣu); or shall I, fallen from both (ubhayacyuta eva), be...? (kim).
The wager: union-drops against world-pleasures, with double-fall risk named.
inference: The wager: union-drops against world-pleasures, with double-fall risk named. The devotee names the risk, not hiding it.
uncertainties: Whether 'ubhayacyuta' means 'fallen from both' or 'fallen from both sides' is unresolved.
Whether 'kim' is a question or a rhetorical exclamation is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: How does devotion join?
premises: Ever (satatam) at Your lotus-feet (bhavaccaraṇāmbujākaracarasya), of me the best hamsa (hi haṃsavarasya) moving in the lake (me).
Above from root below (upari mūlatalād api), and from inside (cāntarād) — may devotion's lotus-stalk (bhaktimṛṇālikā) bend up (upanamatv), unborn (aja) Lord.
Hamsa-and-stalk botany: joining below, inside, above.
inference: Hamsa-and-stalk botany: devotion's lotus-stalk bends up from below, inside, above. Joining at every level.
uncertainties: Whether 'haṃsavarasya' means 'best hamsa' or 'swan-king' is unresolved.
Whether 'bhaktimṛṇālikā' means 'devotion's lotus-stalk' or 'the stalk of devotion' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is scope without seizure?
premises: May all things (samastavastūny api) come under thought's scope (cintāviṣayaṃ) and vision's footing (dṛśaḥ padaṃ ca) for me (mama).
May vision-thought-light-nectar-essences (darśanacintanaprakāśāmṛtasārāṇi) blaze supreme (paraṃ parisphurantu).
Scope, not seizure: all things under thought's scope without seizure.
inference: Scope, not seizure: all things under thought's scope and vision's footing; essences blaze supreme.
uncertainties: Whether 'cintāviṣayaṃ' means 'under thought's scope' or 'as thought's object' is unresolved.
Whether 'parisphurantu' means 'blaze' or 'manifest' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is practice for catastrophe?
premises: Lord (parameśvara), in crashing hardships (teṣu teṣu kṛcchreṣv api), as names bend down (nāmopanamatsv) —
may I be (ahaṃ bhaveyam), fear gone (na paraṃ gatabhīs) only while limb-joined (tvadaṅgasaṅgādupajātādhikasammado), exceeding-joy-mad ('pi yāvat).
Practice for catastrophe: fear gone only while limb-joined, exceeding-joy-mad.
inference: Practice for catastrophe: fear gone only while limb-joined, exceeding-joy-mad. Limb-joined, not doctrine.
uncertainties: Whether 'gatabhīs' means 'fear gone' or 'gone fear' is unresolved.
Whether 'yāvat' means 'while' or 'as long as' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is the closing epistemology?
premises: The universe (viśvam) woven (umbhitaṃ) in Your self (bhavadātmani), shown (prakāśyate) outside (bahiḥ) by You alone (bhavataivāpi) —
what stands firm-certain (yad dṛḍhaniścayopajuṣṭaṃ): may it now shine plain (tad idāniṃ sphuṭam eva bhāsatām).
Closing epistemology: woven in Him, shown by Him, certain — shine.
inference: Closing epistemology: woven in Him, shown by Him, firm-certain — may it now shine plain.
uncertainties: Whether 'umbhitaṃ' means 'woven' or 'born' is unresolved.
Whether 'dṛḍhaniścayopajuṣṭaṃ' modifies 'tat' or 'mahimā' is unresolved.
